findings.title: Universal XSS from website-driven element picker
findings.summary_md: Vendor advisory rated high with no CVE assigned. It says Firefox MV2 uBlock Origin 1.75.2 and lower let a page drive the element picker and add arbitrary trusted filters after one user click when a prevent-xhr or prevent-fetch scriptlet fulfills a response with a WAR. The report reached the vendor on 2026-11-01; fixes appear in 1.75.2, 1.75.4 and 1.76.0 through commits bf69cf7, 9859477, b1f7d27 and 150df12. Credit goes to syvb, and the advisory also notes extraction of the WAR secret on MV2 Chromium.

findings.title: Universal XSS in uBlock Origin from website-driven element picker
findings.summary_md: Researcher Smitty van Bodegom (loops) disclosed a one-click universal XSS in the Firefox MV2 uBlock Origin element picker, plus a less severe variant in MV3 uBO Lite. The chain recovers the per-install extension UUID through a WAR-backed fetch hook, embeds the picker as a hidden `iframe`, and drives it with `postMessage` messages named `epickerStart`, `showDialog` and `resultsetDetails`. A newline in the `opt` field turns the displayed network filter into a second trusted scriptlet filter for another domain; the writeup credits GPT-5.6 Sol with finding the bug and Claude with most of the PoC code. The example relies on the default `lootdest.*##+js(no-fetch-if, adsbygoogle, war:googlesyndication_adsbygoogle.js)` rule and a click on a transparent Create control.

findings.title: Universal XSS in uBlock Origin from website-driven element picker
findings.summary_md: Early news coverage of the iter.ca report and the vendor advisory. It describes the four-stage attack, from internal extension identifier leakage through a hidden picker frame, message channel control, newline filter injection and a captured user click, and lists uBlock Origin and uBO Lite on Manifest V2 Firefox and Manifest V3 as affected. The article reports the fix as a secret password passed from the content script to the picker that rejects messages from outside pages.
